docs.title: PIL Esolang
docs.text:
PIL is a primitive interpreted esolang (esoteric programming language) based off COBOL and assembly. It is a loosely-typed language with no GC.

Here's a factorial example: 

# calculates the factorial of N
factorial(n)
   local result;                 # define a new variable
   leeq n, 1, $0;                # check if N is smaller or equal to 1
   jmp $0, factorial-end;        # if it is, jump to end, where we return 1

   sub n, 1, $1;                 # calculate n-1
   call result, factorial, $1;   # call factorial and store in result
   mul result, n, result;        # calculate the factorial of N
   return result;                # return the result

factorial-end:
   return 1;

main()                           # main is called on start
   factorial 5.0;                # calculate 5!
   println r$0;                  # 120

Think of it like interpreted assembly with functions, returns and higher-level instructions. For more examples check out the Introduction. See Getting Started for installation instructions.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
To run PIL you need the PIL interpreter. There are two options:

  1. download a pre-built executable from Github Releases
  2. build the source code yourself

docs.title: Building
docs.text:
You'll first need to clone the repository or download it as a ZIP. If cloning: 

git clone https://github.com/pil-esolang/PIL.git
cd PIL

The project uses C++20 and can be built using CMake. To build in release: 

cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build
After, the executable will be located in build/pil.

You can also simply build using your favorite compiler: 

g++ -std=c++20 -Iinclude source/*.cpp -o pil

docs.title: Installing globally
docs.text:
To be able to use the interpreter from anywhere on Unix you can move it to /usr/bin: 

sudo mv pil /usr/bin/pil
Then relaunch your terminal and run pil -h to verify.

On Windows you can move the executable to a safe spot (e.g. C:/pil_interpreter/pil.exe) and then add that folder to your path.

docs.title: Hello, World!
docs.text:
To run the famous hello world program paste this into a main.pil file: 

main()
   println "Hello, World!";
And then run using this command: 
pil run main.pil
This should be enough to get you going, good luck!

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
PIL is a loosely-typed language with no GC. It's simple - you can define functions and call them. 

my-func()
   println "Hello, World!";

main()
   my-func; # Hello, World!

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
Comments start with #. There are no multi-line comments in PIL. 

# this is a comment

docs.title: Control flow
docs.text:
There are no control statements (like if-else, for, while, break...), instead you have to define labels and jump to them. 

check-condition(condition)
   jmp condition, check-condition-true;
   println "The condition is false!";
   return;
check-condition-true:
   println "The condition is true!";

main()
   check-condition 1; # The condition is true!
   check-condition 0; # The condition is false!
It's same with loops. Here's a loop that counts from 1 to 10: 
loop(i, n)
loop-start:
   greq i, n, $0;
   jmp $0, loop-end;

   println i;
   incr i;
   goto loop-start;
loop-end:

main()
   loop 1, 10;

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
Variables can be defined inside functions using the local keyword. 

greet()
   local name;
   print "Tell me your name: ";
   readln name;
   printfln "Hello, {}!", name;
   string-free name;

main()
   greet;

docs.title: Including other files
docs.text:
To include a file use @include. It works similarly to C's includes but doesn't require guards:

include.pil 

my-func()
   println "Hello, World!";

main.pil 

@include "include.pil"

main()
   my-func;

docs.title: Structures
docs.text:
PIL also contains structures that can be defined using the struct keyword: 

struct Vec2 ( x, y )

main()
   local v1, v2, v3;
   make Vec2, v1, 1.0, 2.0;
   make Vec2, v2, 3.0, 4.0;

   local x, y;
   add v1.x, v2.x, x;
   add v1.y, v2.y, y;
   make Vec2, v3, x, y;

   printfln "Result: ({}, {})", v3.x, v3.y;
   free v1, v2, v3;

And structures can be used as arrays if necessary using the array keyword: 

struct array MyArray ( _1, _2, _3, _4, _5 )

main()
   local array;
   make MyArray, array, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1;
   println array; # [5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
   array-reverse array;
   println array; # [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
   array-shuffle array;
   println array; # [3, 5, 2, 1, 4] could be something else for you

   local x, y, z;
   array-sort array, 1;
   add array._1, array._2, x;
   add array._3, array._4, y;
   add array._5, array._1, z;
   printfln "[{},{},{}]", x, y, z; # 3, 7, 6
   free array;

docs.title: Enumerations
docs.text:
PIL also contains enumerations: 

enum Day (
   Monday = 1,
   Tuesday,
   Wednesday,
   Thursday,
   Friday,
   Saturday,
   Sunday,
)

main()
   local today, day-names, name;
   array-new day-names, "", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday";
   set Day.Wednesday, today;
   array-at day-names, today, name;
   printfln "Today is {}, {} day of the week.", name, today; # Today is Wednesday, 3 day of the week.
   array-free day-names;

docs.title: Constants and globals
docs.text:
Constants are named values that cannot change. Globals are variables that can be accessed from anywhere. They are defined using const and global keywords respectively. 

const pi = 3.141592;
global r = 10.0;

area()
   local result;
   mul r, r, result;
   mul result, pi, result;
   return result;

main()
   local result;
   call result, area;
   println result; # 314.159
   set 20.0, r;
   call result, area;
   println result; # 1256.637

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text: For a better understanding of the language you can continue reading the documentation. But you learn the best by doing. Check out Getting Started for installation steps.

docs.title: Array library
docs.text: It is recommended to read Language/Values first for a better understanding of allowed parameter types, value semantics and behavior.

docs.title: array-new
docs.text:
Allocate a new array with all values after ARRAY as values. ARRAY - container, ARG1... - any value. 

array-new ARRAY, ARG1, ...

docs.title: array-fill
docs.text:
Fill an array with N VALUEs, allocate it and store it in ARRAY. ARRAY - container, N - unsigned integer, VALUE - any value. 

array-fill ARRAY, N, VALUE

docs.title: array-iota
docs.text:
Fill an array with N incrementing integers starting from START, allocate it and store in ARRAY. ARRAY - container, N - unsigned integer, START - integer. 

array-iota ARRAY, N, START

docs.title: array-clear
docs.text:
Clears array. Its memory will still be available. ARRAY - array. 

array-clear ARRAY

docs.title: array-memfree
docs.text:
Clears array and frees its memory. Does not free the array itself and is not necessary to call it before freeing it. ARRAY - array. 

array-memfree ARRAY

docs.title: array-empty
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if the array is empty, otherwise 0. ARRAY - array, DESTINATION - container. 

array-empty ARRAY, DESTINATION

docs.title: array-size
docs.text:
Stores the size of the array in DESTINATION. ARRAY - array, DESTINATION - container. 

array-size ARRAY, DESTINATION

docs.title: array-capacity
docs.text:
Stores the capacity of the array in DESTINATION. ARRAY - array, DESTINATION - container. 

array-capacity ARRAY, DESTINATION

docs.title: array-reserve
docs.text:
Reserves N capacity for the array to prevent unnecessary reallocations. ARRAY - array, N - unsigned integer. 

array-reserve ARRAY, N

docs.title: array-resize
docs.text:
Resizes array to N values. If the new size is greater than the previous then the empty slots are filled with VALUE. Might reallocate the array. ARRAY - array, N - unsigned integer, VALUE - any value. 

array-resize ARRAY, N, VALUE

docs.title: array-set
docs.text:
Set a value at position N to value VALUE. Throws if N is out of bounds (N < 0 || N >= SIZE). ARRAY - array, N - unsigned integer, VALUE - any value. 

array-set ARRAY, N, VALUE

docs.title: array-at
docs.text:
Get a value at position N and store it in DESTINATION. Throws if N is out of bounds (N < 0 || N >= SIZE). ARRAY - array, N - unsigned integer, DESTINATION - container. 

array-at ARRAY, N, DESTINATION

docs.title: array-back
docs.text:
Get the back (last) value of the array and store it in DESTINATION. Throws if array is empty. ARRAY - array, DESTINATION - container. 

array-back ARRAY, DESTINATION

docs.title: array-front
docs.text:
Get the front (first) value of the array and store it in DESTINATION. Throws if array is empty. ARRAY - array, DESTINATION - container. 

array-front ARRAY, DESTINATION

docs.title: array-push
docs.text:
Push VALUE at the end of the array. Might reallocate the array. ARRAY - array, VALUE - ANY VALUE. 

array-push ARRAY, VALUE

docs.title: array-insert
docs.text:
Insert VALUE at position N in the array. Throws if N is out of bounds (N < 0 || N > SIZE). Might reallocate the array. ARRAY - array, N - unsigned integer, VALUE - any value. 

array-insert ARRAY, N, VALUE

docs.title: array-pop
docs.text:
Pop the last value of the array. Throws if array is empty. ARRAY - array. 

array-pop ARRAY

docs.title: array-erase
docs.text:
Erase the value at position N in the array. Throws if N is out of bounds (N < 0 || N >= SIZE). ARRAY - array, N - unsigned integer. 

array-erase ARRAY, N

docs.title: array-free
docs.text:
Frees all arrays and sets them to null. Does not free arrays' values. Using a freed array will result in an use-after-free error. ARRAY1... - arrays. 

array-free ARRAY1, ...

docs.title: array-deep-free
docs.text:
Frees all arrays and their values recursively and sets them to null. Using a freed array will result in an use-after-free error. ARRAY1... - arrays. 

array-deep-free ARRAY1, ...

docs.title: array-join
docs.text:
Stringify and concatenate all array's values with the CONNECTOR in-between, allocate the result and store it in DESTINATION. Throws if the array contains a map. ARRAY - array, CONNECTOR - stringifyable value, DESTINATION - container. 

array-join ARRAY, CONNECTOR, DESTINATION

docs.title: array-concat
docs.text:
Combine ARRAY1 and ARRAY2 into one, allocate the result and store it in DESTINATION. ARRAY1 - array, ARRAY2 - array, DESTINATION - container. 

array-concat ARRAY1, ARRAY2, DESTINATION

docs.title: array-slice
docs.text:
Slice the array [START; END), allocate the shallow copy and store it in DESTINATION. Throws if START < 0 || START >= SIZE || END < 0 || END > SIZE || START >= END. ARRAY - array, START - unsigned integer, END - unsigned integer, DESTINATION - container. 

array-slice ARRAY, START, END, DESTINATION

docs.title: array-shuffle
docs.text:
Randomly shuffle the array based on global RNG. ARRAY - array. 

array-shuffle ARRAY

docs.title: array-sort
docs.text:
Sort the array. Sorts ascendingly if ASCENDING is truthy, descendingly otherwise. Throws if array contains functions, labels, arrays or maps. ARRAY - array, ASCENDING - integer. 

array-sort ARRAY, ASCENDING

docs.title: array-count
docs.text:
Count the number of times VALUE occurrs in the array and store it in DESTINATION. Time complexity is O(N). ARRAY - array, VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

array-count ARRAY, VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: array-reverse
docs.text:
Reverse the array. Time complexity is O(N/2). ARRAY - array. 

array-reverse ARRAY

docs.title: array-find
docs.text:
Attempts to find the first occurrence of VALUE in the array. Sets DESTINATION to the position if it is found, else null. Time complexity is O(N). ARRAY - array, VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

array-find ARRAY, VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: array-contains
docs.text:
Sets DESTINATION to 1 if VALUE can be found in the array, otherwise 0. Time complexity is O(N). ARRAY - array, VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

array-contains ARRAY, VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: array-erase-all
docs.text:
Erases all VALUEs from array. Time complexity is O(N). ARRAY - array, VALUE - value. 

array-erase-all ARRAY, VALUE

docs.title: array-copy
docs.text:
Shallow copies an array into DESTINATION. Only copies references for complex runtime values like dynamic strings, arrays and maps. ARRAY - array, DESTINATION - container. 

array-copy ARRAY, DESTINATION

docs.title: array-deep-copy
docs.text:
Deep copies an array into DESINATION. Copies all dynamic strings, arrays and maps recursively. If the array contains multiple identical references to the same object, it is only copied once. ARRAY - array, DESTINATION - container. 

array-deep-copy ARRAY, DESTINATION

docs.title: Built-ins
docs.text:
It is recommended to read Language/Values first for a better understanding of allowed parameter types, value semantics and behavior.

These are basic operation/miscellaneous built-ins present in PIL. On top of these, there are some more common math operation built-ins in the Math Library. Unlike other built-in documentation pages, these will contain sub-groups.

docs.title: flush
docs.text:
Flush the output to the terminal. 

flush

docs.title: printch
docs.text:
Output a single character to the terminal. CHAR - character. 

printch CHAR

docs.title: print
docs.text:
Output all ARGS to the terminal. Does not output a separator or a newline. ARGS... - any value. 

print ARGS...

docs.title: println
docs.text:
Output all ARGS to the terminal including a newline. Does not output a separator. ARGS... - any value. 

println ARGS...

docs.title: printf
docs.text:
Formats the FORMAT-STRING string with all arguments after it and outputs it to the terminal. Works by replacing all {} with the arguments in left-to-right direction. Does not validate format argument count. FORMAT-STRING - string, ARG1... - stringifyable value. 

printf FORMAT-STRING, ARG1, ...

docs.title: printfln
docs.text:
Formats the FORMAT-STRING string with all arguments after it and outputs it and a newline to the terminal. Works by replacing all {} with the arguments in left-to-right direction. Does not validate format argument count. FORMAT-STRING - string, ARG1... - stringifyable value. 

printfln FORMAT-STRING, ARG1, ...

docs.title: read
docs.text:
Read a single word (until a whitespace is hit) from the user, allocate it as a string and store it in DESTINATION. DESTINATION - container. 

read DESTINATION

docs.title: readln
docs.text:
Read a whole line (until a newline is hit) from the user, allocate it as a string and store it in DESTINATION. DESTINATION - container. 

readln DESTINATION

docs.title: readch
docs.text:
Read a single character from the user and store it in DESTINATION. Does not output the character to the console nor wait for a newline. DESTINATION - container. 

readch DESTINATION

docs.title: setecho
docs.text:
Set terminal echo based on VALUEs truthiness. 0 - off, otherwise on. When echo is off, nothing is output to the terminal. Does not change behavior of readch. VALUE - any value. 

setecho VALUE

docs.title: le
docs.text:
Checks if A is less than B and if it is, stores 1 in DESTINATION, otherwise 0. Types of A and B must match, although integers can be compared to floats. A - number, character or any string, B - number, character or any string, DESTINATION - container. 

le A, B, DESTINATION

docs.title: gr
docs.text:
Checks if A is greater than B and if it is, stores 1 in DESTINATION, otherwise 0. Types of A and B must match, although integers can be compared to floats. A - number, character or any string, B - number, character or any string, DESTINATION - container. 

gr A, B, DESTINATION

docs.title: leeq
docs.text:
Checks if A is less than or equal to B and if it is, stores 1 in DESTINATION, otherwise 0. Types of A and B must match, although integers can be compared to floats. A - number, character or any string, B - number, character or any string, DESTINATION - container. 

leeq A, B, DESTINATION

docs.title: greq
docs.text:
Checks if A is greater than or equal to B and if it is, stores 1 in DESTINATION, otherwise 0. Types of A and B must match, although integers can be compared to floats. A - number, character or any string, B - number, character or any string, DESTINATION - container. 

greq A, B, DESTINATION

docs.title: eq
docs.text:
Checks if A is equal to B and if it is, stores 1 in DESTINATION, otherwise 0. If A and B don't share the same type 0 is stored, comparing integers to floats is an exception. A - number, character, any string or array, B - number, character, any string or array, DESTINATION - container. 

eq A, B, DESTINATION

docs.title: neq
docs.text:
Checks if A is not equal to B and if it's not, stores 1 in DESTINATION, otherwise 0. If A and B don't share the same type 1 is stored, comparing integers to floats is an exception. A - number, character, any string or array, B - number, character, any string or array, DESTINATION - container. 

neq A, B, DESTINATION

docs.title: and
docs.text:
Checks if both A and B are true and if so, stores 1 in DESTINATION, otherwise 0. A - any value, B - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

and A, B, DESTINATION

docs.title: or
docs.text:
Checks if either A or B is true and if so, stores 1 in DESTINATION, otherwise 0. A - any value, B - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

or A, B, DESTINATION

docs.title: not
docs.text:
Stores the opposite of VALUEs truthiness in DESTINATION - if it is 0, then 1, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

not VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: goto
docs.text:
Unconditionally jumps to LABEL. LABEL - label. 

goto LABEL

docs.title: jmp
docs.text:
Jumps to LABEL if CONDITION is truthy, otherwise does nothing. CONDITION - any value, LABEL - label. 

jmp CONDITION, LABEL

docs.title: jmpn
docs.text:
Jumps to LABEL if CONDITION is not truthy, otherwise does nothing. CONDITION - any value, LABEL - label. 

jmpn CONDITION, LABEL

docs.title: jmptable
docs.text:
Checks VALUE against all TARGETs and if there is a match, then jump to the label after it. If the passed argument count is even and there are no matches, jump to DEFAULT-LABEL, otherwise do nothing. Each TARGET must have a corresponding LABEL after it. VALUE - number, character, any string or array, TARGET... - number, character, any string or array, LABEL... - label, DEFAULT-LABEL? - optional label. 

jmptable VALUE, TARGET, LABEL..., DEFAULT-LABEL?

docs.title: call
docs.text:
Calls FUNCTION with given arguments ARGS... (if any) and stores all of the returns in RETURNS... (if any). Throws if ARGS... count does not match FUNCTIONs arity or if FUNCTION is not parse-time. For runtime function calls use func-call. Throws a warning if RETURNS... count does not match actual returned value count. RETURNS... - containers, FUNCTION - function, ARGS... - any value. 

call RETURNS..., FUNCTION, ARGS...

docs.title: func-call
docs.text:
Calls FUNCTION with given arguments ARGS... (if any). Throws if ARGS... count does not match FUNCTION's arity. FUNCTION - function, ARGS... - any value. 

func-call FUNCTION, ARGS...

docs.title: return
docs.text:
Returns from the function and stores all VALUES... (if any) in return registers. Exits the program if called from main function. VALUES... - any value. 

return VALUES...

docs.title: catch
docs.text:
Calls FUNCTION with given arguments ARGS... (if any) and allocates and stores all errors as an array of strings in DESTINATION if any were thrown, otherwise stores null. Throws if ARGS... count does not match FUNCTION's arity. DESTINATION - container, FUNCTION - function, ARGS... - any value. 

catch DESTINATION, FUNCTION, ARGS...

docs.title: assert
docs.text:
Exits the program and formats the FORMAT-STRING in the same manner as printf if CONDITION is not truthy. Does not precompute the message if the CONDITION is truthy. CONDITION - any value, FORMAT-STRING - string, ARGS... - stringifyable value. 

assert CONDITION, FORMAT-STRING, ARGS...

docs.title: warn
docs.text:
Formats the FORMAT-STRING in the same manner as printf and outputs it as a warning. FORMAT-STRING - string, ARGS... - stringifyable value. 

warn FORMAT-STRING, ARGS...

docs.title: error
docs.text:
Formats the FORMAT-STRING in the same manner as printf, outputs it as an error and as long as the error isn't caught using catch, exits the program. FORMAT-STRING - string, ARGS... - stringifyable value. 

error FORMAT-STRING, ARGS...

docs.title: exit
docs.text:
Unconditionally exits the program with exit code CODE. An erroneous code is any code except for 0. CODE - number. 

exit CODE

docs.title: stack-depth
docs.text:
Stores the depth of the stack in DESTINATION. DESTINATION - container. 

stack-depth DESTINATION

docs.title: stack-name
docs.text:
Allocates and stores the name of the calee's function in DESTINATION. DESTINATION - container. 

stack-name DESTINATION

docs.title: stack-line
docs.text:
Stores the line of calee's function in DESTINATION. DESTINATION - container. 

stack-line DESTINATION

docs.title: stack-file
docs.text:
Allocates and stores the name of the file of the calee's function in DESTINATION. DESTINATION - container. 

stack-file DESTINATION

docs.title: stack-trace
docs.text:
Dumps the stack trace and exits the program. 

stack-trace

docs.title: typeof
docs.text:
Allocates and stores the name of the type of VALUE in DESTINATION. Integer - int, float - float, character - char, constant and dynamic strings - string, array - array, map - map, function - function, label - label, null - null. VALUE - any value. DESTINATION - container. 

typeof VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-num
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is a number, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-num VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-float
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is a float, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-float VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-int
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is an integer, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-int VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-char
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is a character, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-char VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-string
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is a string, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-string VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-dynamic-string
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is a dynamically allocated string, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-dynamic-string VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-constant-string
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is a constant string, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-constant-string VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-array
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is an array, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-array VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-map
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is a map, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-map VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-file-handle
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is a file handle, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-file-handle VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-reg
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is a container, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-reg VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-function
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is a function, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-function VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-label
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is a label, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-label VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-struct
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is a structure, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-struct VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-of-struct
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is of struct STRUCT, otherwise 0. VALUE - array, STRUCT - structure, DESTINATION - container. 

is-of-struct VALUE, STRUCT, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-null
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is null, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-null VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-inf
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is a float and infinite, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-inf VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: is-nan
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if VALUE is a float and NaN, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

is-nan VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: to-int
docs.text:
Converts VALUE to an integer and stores it in DESTINATION. If VALUE is a string and it isn't a valid number or is out of bounds, store null instead. VALUE - number, character or string, DESTINATION - container. 

to-int VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: to-float
docs.text:
Converts VALUE to a float and stores it in DESTINATION. If VALUE is a string and it isn't a valid number or is out of bounds, store null instead. VALUE - number, character or string, DESTINATION - container. 

to-float VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: to-char
docs.text:
Converts VALUE to a character and stores it in DESTINATION. VALUE - number or character. DESTINATION - container. 

to-char VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: time
docs.text:
Stores the elapsed time in milliseconds since the first time call in DESTINATION. DESTINATION - container. 

time DESTINATION

docs.title: unix-time
docs.text:
Stores seconds since epoch in DESTINATION. DESTINATION - container. 

unix-time DESTINATION

docs.title: date
docs.text:
Formats and allocates a date based on FORMAT-STRING. All format options are available here. All of them are available and are prefixed with %. FORMAT-STRING - string, DESTINATION - container. 

date FORMAT-STRING, DESTINATION

docs.title: sleep
docs.text:
Sleep for SECONDS seconds. SECONDS - number. 

sleep SECONDS

docs.title: swap
docs.text:
Swap both values in the given containers. A - container, B - container. 

swap A, B

docs.title: set
docs.text:
Store VALUE in DESTINATION. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

set VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: valtable
docs.text:
Checks VALUE against all TARGETs and if there is a match, store the value after the TARGET in DESTINATION. Otherwise if there is an odd number of arguments, store DEFAULT?, else null. Each TARGET must have a RESULT after it. VALUE - any value except for map, DESTINATION - container, TARGET... - any value except for map, RESULT... - any value, DEFAULT? - optional value. 

valtable VALUE, DESTINATION, TARGET, RESULT, ..., DEFAULT?

docs.title: table-contains
docs.text:
Checks whether VALUE matches any of the values and stores 1 in DESTINATION if it does, otherwise 0. VALUE - any value except for map, DESTINATION - container, TARGET... - any value except for map. 

table-contains VALUE, DESTINATION, TARGET...

docs.title: reg-size
docs.text:
Stores the total number of registers in DESTINATION. DESTINATION - container. 

reg-size DESTINATION

docs.title: reg-at
docs.text:
Get the value of the register at position ID and store it in DESTINATION. Throws if ID is out of bounds. ID - unsigned integer, DESTINATION - container. 

reg-at ID, DESTINATION

docs.title: reg-set
docs.text:
Set the register at position ID to VALUE. Throws if ID is out of bounds. ID - unsigned integer, VALUE - any value. 

reg-set ID, VALUE

docs.title: return-reg-size
docs.text:
Stores the total number of return registers in DESTINATION. DESTINATION - container. 

return-reg-size DESTINATION

docs.title: return-reg-at
docs.text:
Get the value of the return register at position ID and store it in DESTINATION. Throws if ID is out of bounds. ID - unsigned integer, DESTINATION - container. 

return-reg-at ID, DESTINATION

docs.title: return-reg-set
docs.text:
Set the return register at position ID to VALUE. Throws if ID is out of bounds. ID - unsigned integer, VALUE - any value. 

return-reg-set ID, VALUE

docs.title: return-count
docs.text:
Stores the number of values returned by the last function call in DESTINATION. DESTINATION - container. 

return-count DESTINATION

docs.title: func-arity
docs.text:
Stores the parameter count of FUNCTION in DESTINATION. FUNCTION - function, DESTINATION - container. 

func-arity FUNCTION, DESTINATION

docs.title: func-variadic
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if FUNCTION is variadic, otherwise 0. FUNCTION - function, DESTINATION - container. 

func-variadic FUNCTION, DESTINATION

docs.title: func-arg-match
docs.text:
Checks whether ARGS would be a valid argument count for FUNCTION and stores 1 in DESTINATION if so, otherwise 0. FUNCTION - function, ARGS - unsigned integer, DESTINATION - container. 

func-arg-match FUNCTION, ARGS, DESTINATION

docs.title: make
docs.text:
Create a new structure based on STRUCT template and store in DESTINATION. ARGS... count must match structure's field count. STRUCT - structure, DESTINATION - container, ARGS... - any value. 

make STRUCT, DESTINATION, ARGS...

docs.title: free
docs.text:
Deallocates all values. Throws if an argument is not an allocated value. ARGS... - string, array or map. 

free ARGS...

docs.title: deep-free
docs.text:
Deallocates all values and deallocates all children recursively if container has any. Throws if an argument is not an allocated value. ARGS... - string, array or map. 

deep-free ARGS...

docs.title: copy
docs.text:
Shallow copy VALUE to DESTINATION. Allocates the value if it is allocated. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

copy VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: deep-copy
docs.text:
Deep copy VALUE to DESTINATION. Allocates the value if it is allocated and all its children. If the container contains multiple identical references to the same object, it is only copied once. VALUE - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

deep-copy VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: size
docs.text:
Takes and stores the size of VALUE in DESTINATION. If VALUE is not a container, stores 1. VALUE - any value. DESTINATION - container. 

size VALUE, DESTINATION

docs.title: at
docs.text:
Stores the value at KEY in DESTINATION. For maps KEY is the literal key and for arrays and strings it is the index. Throws if key is of incorrect type (non-integer for strings and arrays or non-key type for maps) or if it is out of bounds. Throws if CONTAINER cannot be accessed. CONTAINER - string, array or map, KEY - integer/key value, DESTINATION - container. 

at CONTAINER, KEY, DESTINATION

docs.title: store
docs.text:
Store VALUE at KEY. For maps KEY is the literal key and for arrays and strings it is the index. Throws if key is of incorrect type (non-integer for strings and arrays or non-key type for maps) or if it is out of bounds. Throws if CONTAINER cannot be accessed. CONTAINER - dynamic string, array or map, KEY - integer/key value, VALUE - any value. 

store CONTAINER, KEY, VALUE

docs.title: File & OS library
docs.text:
It is recommended to read Language/Values first for a better understanding of allowed parameter types, value semantics and behavior.

Most of these built-ins require special permissions that can be passed to the interpreter as flags. Without them, the program won't run. This is in place to prevent accidental malicious code execution.

docs.title: file-open
docs.text:
Try to open PATH in mode MODE and store the file handle in DESTINATION on success or null value on failure. Mode R - read only, W - write only, A - write only (append), X - read and write. Throws on unknown mode. PATH - string, MODE - character, DESTINATION - container.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

file-open PATH, MODE, DESTINATION

docs.title: file-close
docs.text:
Close file FILE and set the handle to null. FILE - file handle.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

file-close FILE

docs.title: file-read
docs.text:
Read the whole contents of FILE, allocate it and store in DESTINATION. FILE - file handle, DESTINATION - container.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

file-read FILE, DESTINATION

docs.title: file-readln
docs.text:
Read a line from FILE, allocate it and store in DESTINATION. FILE - file handle, DESTINATION - container.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

file-readln FILE, DESTINATION

docs.title: file-readch
docs.text:
Read a single character from FILE and store in DESTINATION. FILE - file handle, DESTINATION - container.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

file-readch FILE, DESTINATION

docs.title: file-read-bytes
docs.text:
Read N bytes from FILE, allocate them and store as a dynamic string in DESTINATION. FILE - file handle, N - unsigned integer, DESTINATION - container.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

file-read-bytes FILE, N, DESTINATION

docs.title: file-eof
docs.text:
Store 1 in DESTINATION if EOF is found, else 0. FILE - file handle, DESTINATION - container.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

file-eof FILE, DESTINATION

docs.title: file-write
docs.text:
Write stringified DATA to FILE. FILE - file handle, DATA - stringifyable value.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

file-write FILE, DATA

docs.title: file-writeln
docs.text:
Write stringified DATA to FILE and append a newline. FILE - file handle, DATA - stringifyable value.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

file-writeln FILE, DATA

docs.title: file-flush
docs.text:
Flush the output to FILE. FILE - file handle.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

file-flush FILE

docs.title: file-tell
docs.text:
Store the current position in FILE (in bytes from the start of the file) in DESTINATION. Throws if the stream is in a failed state. FILE - file handle, DESTINATION - container.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

file-tell FILE, DESTINATION

docs.title: file-seek
docs.text:
Move the position in FILE to POS bytes from the start of the file. Clears any EOF or error state on the stream. FILE - file handle, POS - unsigned integer.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

file-seek FILE, POS

docs.title: file-seek-rel
docs.text:
Move the position in FILE by OFFSET bytes relative to the current position. A negative OFFSET moves backwards. Clears any EOF or error state on the stream. FILE - file handle, OFFSET - integer.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

file-seek-rel FILE, OFFSET

docs.title: file-seek-end
docs.text:
Move the position in FILE by OFFSET bytes relative to the end of the file. Clears any EOF or error state on the stream. FILE - file handle, OFFSET - integer.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

file-seek-end FILE, OFFSET

docs.title: path-exists
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if PATH exists, otherwise 0. PATH - string, DESTINATION - container.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

path-exists PATH, DESTINATION

docs.title: path-is-file
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if PATH exists and is a regular file, otherwise 0. PATH - string, DESTINATION - container.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

path-is-file PATH, DESTINATION

docs.title: path-is-dir
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if PATH exists and is a directory, otherwise 0. PATH - string, DESTINATION - contaienr.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

path-is-dir PATH, DESTINATION

docs.title: path-size
docs.text:
Stores the size PATH in DESTINATION. Stores null if PATH is a directory. Can throw. PATH - string, DESTINATION - container.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

path-size PATH, DESTINATION

docs.title: path-modified-time
docs.text:
Stores the last modified time of PATH in DESTINATION. Can throw. PATH - string, DESTINATION - container.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

path-modified-time PATH, DESTINATION

docs.title: path-create-dir
docs.text:
Recursively creates directories based on PATH. Can throw. PATH - string.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

path-create-dir PATH

docs.title: path-remove
docs.text:
Remove a file or an empty directory based on PATH. Can throw. PATH - string.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

path-remove PATH

docs.title: path-remove-all
docs.text:
Remove files and directories recursively based on PATH. Can throw. PATH - string.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

path-remove-all PATH

docs.title: path-copy
docs.text:
Copy PATH to DESTINATION. Can throw. PATH - string, DESTINATION - string.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

path-copy PATH, DESTINATION

docs.title: path-move
docs.text:
Move PATH to DESTINATION. Can throw. PATH - string, DESTINATION - string.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

path-move PATH, DESTINATION

docs.title: path-join
docs.text:
Join both paths together, allocate it and store in DESTINATION. PATH1 - string, PATH2 - string, DESTINATION - container. 

path-join PATH1, PATH2, DESTINATION

docs.title: path-filename
docs.text:
Allocate the filename of the path (dir/file.ext -> file.ext) and store it in DESTINATION. PATH - string, DESTINATION - container. 

path-filename PATH, DESTINATION

docs.title: path-stem
docs.text:
Allocate the stem of the path (dir/file.ext -> file) and store it in DESTINATION. PATH - string, DESTINATION - container. 

path-stem PATH, DESTINATION

docs.title: path-extension
docs.text:
Allocate the extension of the path (dir/file.ext -> .ext) and store it in DESTINATION. Files with extensions return their extension starting with a dot, whereas files with no extension will return an empty string. PATH - string, DESTINATION - container. 

path-extension PATH, DESTINATION

docs.title: path-parent
docs.text:
Allocate the parent of the path (dir/file.ext -> dir/) and store it in DESTINATION. Returns a copy of PATH if no parent is present. PATH - string, DESTINATION - container. 

path-parent PATH, DESTINATION

docs.title: path-absolute
docs.text:
Allocate the absolute path of PATH and store it in DESTINATION. PATH - string, DESTINATION - container. 

path-absolute PATH, DESTINATION

docs.title: path-normalize
docs.text:
Allocate the lexically normal path of PATH and store it in DESTINATION. PATH - string, DESTINATION - container. 

path-normalize PATH, DESTINATION

docs.title: dir-list
docs.text:
Allocate an array of all paths of files and directories found in PATH and store it in DESTINATION. PATH - string, DESTINATION - container.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

dir-list PATH, DESTINATION

docs.title: dir-list-recursive
docs.text:
Allocate an array of all paths of files and directories recursively found in PATH and store it in DESTINATION. PATH - string, DESTINATION - container.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

dir-list-recursive PATH, DESTINATION

docs.title: os-name
docs.text:
Allocate and return the name of the user's OS. Windows - windows, MacOS - macos, Linux - linux, any other OS - unknown. DESTINATION - container. 

os-name DESTINATION

docs.title: os-cwd
docs.text:
Allocate the current working directory and store in DESTINATION. Can throw. DESTINATION - container.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

os-cwd DESTINATION

docs.title: os-set-cwd
docs.text:
Set the current working directory to PATH. Can throw. PATH - string.

Must have file I/O permissions. 

os-set-cwd PATH

docs.title: os-env-get
docs.text:
Get environment variable VAR and store it in DESTINATION. Stores null if it doesn't exist. VAR - string, DESTINATION - container.

Must have environment permissions. 

os-env-get VAR, DESTINATION

docs.title: os-env-set
docs.text:
Set environment variable VAR to stringified value VALUE. VAR - string, VALUE - stringifyable value.

Must have environment permissions. 

os-env-set VAR, VALUE

docs.title: os-exec
docs.text:
Execute command COMMAND and store any output up until 4KiB in DESTINATION. Throws if cannot open pipe. COMMAND - string, DESTINATION - container.

Must have command execution permissions. 

os-exec COMMAND, DESTINATION

docs.title: os-exit-code
docs.text:
Stores the last exit code from os-exec in DESTINATION. By default it is 0. DESTINATION - container. 

os-exit-code DESTINATION

docs.title: Map library
docs.text: It is recommended to read Language/Values first for a better understanding of allowed parameter types, value semantics and behavior.

docs.title: map-new
docs.text:
Allocate a new map with all key-value pairs after MAP set. Throws if passed argument count is even. MAP - container, KEY1 - key value, VALUE1 - any value. 

map-new MAP, KEY1, VALUE1, ...

docs.title: map-erase
docs.text:
Erase a key-value pair from the map based on the KEY. Does nothing if it does not exist. MAP - map, KEY - key value. 

map-erase MAP, KEY

docs.title: map-set
docs.text:
Set or insert a VALUE with the key KEY. MAP - map, KEY - key value, VALUE - any value. 

map-set MAP, KEY, VALUE

docs.title: map-at
docs.text:
Get the value at key KEY and store it in DESTINATION. If there is no value at KEY, store null. MAP - map, KEY - key value, DESTINATION - container. 

map-at MAP, KEY, DESTINATION

docs.title: map-at-or
docs.text:
Get the value at key KEY and store it in DESTINATION. If there is no value at KEY, add it with the value set to DEFAULT and store it in DESTINATION. MAP - map, KEY - key value, DEFAULT - any value, DESTINATION - container. 

map-at-or MAP, KEY, DEFAULT, DESTINATION

docs.title: map-contains
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if a key-value pair with key KEY exists, otherwise 0. MAP - map, KEY - key value, DESTINATION - container. 

map-contains MAP, KEY, DESTINATION

docs.title: map-size
docs.text:
Stores the size of the map in DESTINATION. MAP - map, DESTINATION - container. 

map-size MAP, DESTINATION

docs.title: map-empty
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if the map is empty, otherwise 0. MAP - map, DESTINATION - container. 

map-empty MAP, DESTINATION

docs.title: map-clear
docs.text:
Clears all key-value pairs. MAP - map. 

map-clear MAP

docs.title: map-keys
docs.text:
Gets all map's keys, allocates an array of them and stores in DESTINATION. MAP - map, DESTINATION - container. 

map-keys MAP, DESTINATION

docs.title: map-values
docs.text:
Gets all map's values, allocates an array of them and stores in DESTINATION. MAP - map, DESTINATION - container. 

map-values MAP, DESTINATION

docs.title: map-merge
docs.text:
Merge MAP1 and MAP2 and store the result in DESTINATION. MAP2's values have higher priority. MAP1 - map, MAP2 - map, DESTINATION - container. 

map-merge MAP1, MAP2, DESTINATION

docs.title: map-free
docs.text:
Frees all maps and sets them to null. Does not free maps' key-value pairs. Using a free map will result in an use-after-free error. MAP1... - maps. 

map-free MAP1, ...

docs.title: map-deep-free
docs.text:
Frees all maps and their key-value pairs recursively and sets them to null. Using a freed map will result in an use-after-free error. MAP1... - maps. 

map-deep-free MAP1, ...

docs.title: map-copy
docs.text:
Shallow copies a map into DESTINATION. Only copies references for complex runtime values like dynamic strings, arrays and maps. MAP - map, DESTINATION - container. 

map-copy MAP, DESTINATION

docs.title: map-deep-copy
docs.text:
Deep copies a map into DESTINATION. Copies all dynamic strings, arrays and maps recursively. If the map contains multiple identical references to the same object, it is only copied once. MAP - map, DESTINATION - container. 

map-deep-copy MAP, DESTINATION

docs.title: Math Library
docs.text: It is recommended to read Language/Values first for a better understanding of allowed parameter types, value semantics and behavior.

docs.title: incr
docs.text:
Increment the value stored in NUMBER. NUMBER - container containing a number. 

incr NUMBER

docs.title: decr
docs.text:
Decrement the value stored in NUMBER. NUMBER - container containing a number. 

decr NUMBER

docs.title: sum
docs.text:
Add all numbers together and store in RESULT. Returns float if at least a single value is a float. N1... - number, RESULT - container. 

sum N1, N2, ..., RESULT

docs.title: add
docs.text:
Add N1 and N2 together and store in RESULT. Returns float if either number is a float. N1 - number, N2 - number, RESULT - container. 

add N1, N2, RESULT

docs.title: sub
docs.text:
Subtract N1 by N2 and store in RESULT. Returns float if either number is a float. N1 - number, N2 - number, RESULT - container. 

sub N1, N2, RESULT

docs.title: mul
docs.text:
Multiply N1 and N2 together and store in RESULT. Returns float if either number is a float. N1 - number, N2 - number, RESULT - container. 

mul N1, N2, RESULT

docs.title: div
docs.text:
Divide N1 by N2 and store in RESULT. Returns float if either number is a float. Returns 0 on division by zero. N1 - number, N2 - number, RESULT - container. 

div N1, N2, RESULT

docs.title: mod
docs.text:
Get the remainder of dividing N1 by N2 and store in RESULT. Supports floats and negative numbers. Returns float if either number is a float. Returns 0 on division by zero. N1 - number, N2 - number, RESULT - container. 

mod N1, N2, RESULT

docs.title: fmod
docs.text:
Get the remainder of dividing N1 by N2, using the formula ((N1 % N2) + N2) % N2, and store in RESULT. Supports floats and negative numbers. Returns float if either number is a float. Returns 0 on division by zero. N1 - number, N2 - number, RESULT - container. 

fmod N1, N2, RESULT

docs.title: pow
docs.text:
Exponentiate N1 to the exponent N2. Returns float if either number is a float. N1 - number, N2 - number, RESULT - container. 

pow N1, N2, RESULT

docs.title: neg
docs.text:
Negate N and store in RESULT. N - number, RESULT - container. 

neg N, RESULT

docs.title: sqrt
docs.text:
Get the square root of N and store in RESULT. Returns float. Returns NAN if N is negative. N - number, RESULT - container. 

sqrt N, RESULT

docs.title: cbrt
docs.text:
Get the cube root of N and store in RESULT. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

cbrt N, RESULT

docs.title: sin
docs.text:
Get the sine of N and store in RESULT. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

sin N, RESULT

docs.title: cos
docs.text:
Get the cosine of N and store in RESULT. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

cos N, RESULT

docs.title: tan
docs.text:
Get the tangent of N and store in RESULT. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

tan N, RESULT

docs.title: asin
docs.text:
Get the arcsine of N and store in RESULT. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

asin N, RESULT

docs.title: acos
docs.text:
Get the arccosine of N and store in RESULT. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

acos N, RESULT

docs.title: atan
docs.text:
Get the arctangent of N and store in RESULT. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

atan N, RESULT

docs.title: atan2
docs.text:
Get the arctangent of Y / X using the signs of arguments to determine the correct quadrant and store in RESULT. Returns float. Y - number, X - number, RESULT - container. 

atan2 Y, X, RESULT

docs.title: asinh
docs.text:
Get the inverse hyperbolic sine of N and store in RESULT. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

asinh N, RESULT

docs.title: acosh
docs.text:
Get the inverse hyperbolic cosine of N and store in RESULT. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

acosh N, RESULT

docs.title: atanh
docs.text:
Get the inverse hyperbolic tangent of N and store in RESULT. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

atanh N, RESULT

docs.title: sinh
docs.text:
Get the hyperbolic sine of N and store in RESULT. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

sinh N, RESULT

docs.title: cosh
docs.text:
Get the hyperbolic cosine of N and store in RESULT. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

cosh N, RESULT

docs.title: tanh
docs.text:
Get the hyperbolic tangent of N and store in RESULT. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

tanh N, RESULT

docs.title: abs
docs.text:
Get the absolute value of N and store in RESULT. N - number, RESULT - container. 

abs N, RESULT

docs.title: min
docs.text:
Get the minimum value of N1 and N2 and store in RESULT. Returns float if either value is a float. N1 - number, N2 - number, RESULT - container. 

min N1, N2, RESULT

docs.title: max
docs.text:
Get the maximum value of N1 and N2 and store in RESULT. Returns float if either value is a float. N1 - number, N2 - number, RESULT - container. 

max N1, N2, RESULT

docs.title: clamp
docs.text:
Clamp X to range [LO; HI] and store in RESULT. Returns float if any value is a float. Throws if LO > HI. X - number, LO - number, HI - number, RESULT - container. 

clamp X, LO, HI, RESULT

docs.title: sign
docs.text:
Get the sign of N and store in RESULT. Returns integer. N - number, RESULT - container. 

sign N, RESULT

docs.title: trunc
docs.text:
Truncate float N and store in RESULT. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

trunc N, RESULT

docs.title: ceil
docs.text:
Round float N to the smallest integer not less than N. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

ceil N, RESULT

docs.title: floor
docs.text:
Round float N to the largest integer not greater than N. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

floor N, RESULT

docs.title: round
docs.text:
Round float N to the nearest integer. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

round N, RESULT

docs.title: exp
docs.text:
Computes Euler's number raised to the power N. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

exp N, RESULT

docs.title: ln
docs.text:
Computes the natural (base e) logarithm of N. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

ln N, RESULT

docs.title: log
docs.text:
Computes the base B logarithm of N, using formula ln(N) / ln(B). Returns float. N - number, B - number, RESULT - container. 

log N, B, RESULT

docs.title: log2
docs.text:
Computes the base 2 logarithm of N. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

log2 N, RESULT

docs.title: log10
docs.text:
Computes the base 10 logarithm of N. Returns float. N - number, RESULT - container. 

log10 N, RESULT

docs.title: lerp
docs.text:
Linearly interpolate A to B based on T. Returns float. A - number, B - number, T - number, RESULT - container. 

lerp A, B, T, RESULT

docs.title: step-towards
docs.text:
Step towards TARGET by 1 until it is reached. Returns float if either value is a float. N - number, TARGET - number, RESULT - container. 

step-towards N, TARGET, RESULT

docs.title: seed-random
docs.text:
Seed the global RNG used in all random operations, like random, randf-range, randi-range and array-shuffle. SEED - unsigned integer. 

seed-random SEED

docs.title: random
docs.text:
Get a random float in range [0; 1) based on global RNG and store in RESULT. RESULT - container. 

random RESULT

docs.title: randf-range
docs.text:
Get a random float in range [MIN; MAX) based on global RNG and store in RESULT. Throws if MIN > MAX. MIN - number, MAX - number, RESULT - result. 

randf-range MIN, MAX, RESULT

docs.title: randi-range
docs.text:
Get a random integer in range [MIN; MAX] based on global RNG and store in RESULT. Throws if MIN > MAX. MIN - number, MAX - number, RESULT - result. 

randi-range MIN, MAX, RESULT

docs.title: gcd

gcd N1, N2, RESULT

docs.title: lcm

lcm N1, N2, RESULT

docs.title: hypot3

hypot X, Y, Z, RESULT

docs.title: bit-and
docs.text:
Perform bitwise and operation on N1 and N2 and store in RESULT. N1 - unsigned integer, N2 - unsigned integer, RESULT - container. 

bit-and N1, N2, RESULT

docs.title: bit-or

Perform bitwise or operation on N1 and N2 and store in RESULT. N1 - unsigned integer, N2 - unsigned integer, RESULT - container. 

bit-or N1, N2, RESULT

docs.title: bit-xor
docs.text:
Perform bitwise inclusive or operation on N1 and N2 and store in RESULT. N1 - unsigned integer, N2 - unsigned integer, RESULT - container. 

bit-xor N1, N2, RESULT

docs.title: bit-not

Perform bitwise not operation on N1 and store in RESULT. N1 - unsigned integer, RESULT - container. 

bit-not N1, RESULT

docs.title: bit-shl

docs.title: bit-shr

Perform bitwise shift right operation on N1 and N2 and store in RESULT. Throws if N2 >= 64. N1 - unsigned integer, N2 - unsigned integer, RESULT - container. 

bit-shr N1, N2, RESULT

docs.title: bit-count

Return the count of set bits in N and store in RESULT. N - unsigned integer, RESULT - container. 

bit-count N, RESULT

docs.title: bit-test

docs.title: bit-set

bit-set A, N, RESULT

docs.title: bit-clear

docs.title: bit-toggle
docs.text:

docs.title: String library
docs.text: It is recommended to read Language/Values first for a better understanding of allowed parameter types, value semantics and behavior.

docs.title: string-new
docs.text:
Stringifies and concatenates all arguments after DESTINATION, allocates a new string and stores it in DESTINATION. DESTINATION - container, ARGS... - stringifyable values. 

string-new DESTINATION, ARGS, ...

docs.title: string-format
docs.text:
Formats the FORMAT-STRING string with all arguments after it, allocates a new string and stores it in DESTINATION. Works by replacing all {} with the arguments in left-to-right direction. Does not validate format argument count. DESTINATION - container, FORMAT-STRING - string, ARGS... - stringifyable values. 

string-format DESTINATION, FORMAT-STRING, ARGS, ...

docs.title: string-repeat
docs.text:
Stringifies STRING, allocates a new string that is STRING repeated N times and stores it in DESTINATION. DESTINATION - container, N - unsigned integer, STRING - stringifyable value. 

string-repeat DESTINATION, N, STRING

docs.title: string-clear
docs.text:
Clears string. Its memory will still be available. STRING - dynamic string. 

string-clear STRING

docs.title: string-memfree
docs.text:
Clears string and frees its memory. Does not free the string itself and is not necessary to call it before freeing it. STRING - dynamic string. 

string-memfree STRING

docs.title: string-empty
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if the string is empty, otherwise 0. STRING - string, DESTINATION - container. 

string-empty STRING, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-size
docs.text:
Stores the size of the string in DESTINATION. STRING - string, DESTINATION - container. 

string-size STRING, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-capacity
docs.text:
Stores the capacity (the maximum size before a reallocation) of the string in DESTINATION. STRING - string, DESTINATION - container. 

string-capacity STRING, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-reserve
docs.text:
Reserves N capacity for the string to prevent unnecessary reallocations. STRING - dynamic string, N - unsigned integer. 

string-reserve STRING, N

docs.title: string-resize
docs.text:
Resizes string to N characters. If the new size is greater than the previous then the empty slots are filled with CHAR. Might reallocate the string. STRING - dynamic string, N - unsigned integer, CHAR - character. 

string-resize STRING, N, CHAR

docs.title: string-set
docs.text:
Set a character at position N to character CHAR. Throws if N is out of bounds (N < 0 || N >= SIZE). STRING - dynamic string, N - unsigned integer, CHAR - character. 

string-set STRING, N, CHAR

docs.title: string-at
docs.text:
Get a character at position N and store it in DESTINATION. Throws if N is out of bounds (N < 0 || N >= SIZE). STRING - string, N - unsigned integer, DESTINATION - container. 

string-at STRING, N, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-back
docs.text:
Get the back (last) character of the string and store it in DESTINATION. Throws if string is empty. STRING - string, DESTINATION - container. 

string-back STRING, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-front
docs.text:
Get the front (first) character of the string and store it in DESTINATION. Throws if string is empty. STRING - string, DESTINATION - container. 

string-front STRING, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-push
docs.text:
Push CHAR at the end of the string. Might reallocate the string. STRING - dynamic string, CHAR - character. 

string-push STRING, CHAR

docs.title: string-insert
docs.text:
Insert CHAR at position N in the string. Throws if N is out of bounds (N < 0 || N > SIZE). Might reallocate the string. STRING - dynamic string, N - unsigned integer, CHAR - character. 

string-insert STRING, N, CHAR

docs.title: string-pop
docs.text:
Pop the last character of the string. Throws if string is empty. STRING - dynamic string. 

string-pop STRING

docs.title: string-erase
docs.text:
Erase a character at position N in the string. Throws if N is out of bounds (N < 0 || N >= SIZE). STRING - dynamic string, N - unsigned integer. 

string-erase STRING, N

docs.title: string-free
docs.text:
Frees all strings and sets their values to null. Using a freed string will result in an use-after-free error. STRING1... - dynamic strings. 

string-free STRING1, ...

docs.title: string-split
docs.text:
Split the string on DELIMITER, allocate an array of the split pieces and store it in DESTINATION. Time complexity is O(N*M). Throws if DELIMITER is empty. STRING - string, DELIMITER - string or character, DESTINATION - container. 

string-split STRING, DELIMITER, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-concat
docs.text:
Stringifies and concatenate all values after STRING to the string. STRING - dynamic string, ARG1... - any values except for maps. 

string-concat STRING, ARG1, ...

docs.title: string-substr
docs.text:
Creates a substring [START; END) from the given string and saves it in DESTINATION. Throws if START < 0 || START >= SIZE || END < 0 || END > SIZE || START >= END. STRING - string, START - unsigned integer, END - unsigned integer, DESTINATION - container. 

string-substr STRING, START, END, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-count
docs.text:
Counts the number of occurrences of TARGET in the string and stores it in DESTINATION. Time complexity if TARGET is a character is O(N), whereas if TARGET is a string, the complexity is O(N + M), where M is the size of the target string. STRING - string, TARGET - string or character, DESTINATION - container. 

string-count STRING, TARGET, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-reverse
docs.text:
Reverses the string. Time complexity is O(N/2). STRING - dynamic string. 

string-reverse STRING

docs.title: string-find
docs.text:
Attempts to find TARGET in the string starting from position START (0 to search everything). Returns position if target can be found, otherwise null. Time complexity is O(N*M). Throws if START < 0 || START > SIZE. STRING - string, TARGET - string or character, START - unsigned integer, DESTINATION - container. 

string-find STRING, TARGET, START, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-rfind
docs.text:
Attempts to find TARGET in the string starting from position START (>=SIZE or -1 to search everything) in a reverse order. Returns position if target can be found, otherwise null. Time complexity is O(N*M). STRING - string, TARGET - string or character, START - unsigned integer, DESTINATION - container. 

string-rfind STRING, TARGET, START, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-find-first-of
docs.text:
Attempts to find the first character found in TARGET in the string. Returns position if target can be found, otherwise null. Time complexity is O(N*M). STRING - string, TARGET - string, DESTINATION - container. 

string-find-first-of STRING, TARGET, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-find-first-not-of
docs.text:
Attempts to find the first character not found in TARGET in the string. Returns position if target can be found, otherwise null. Time complexity is O(N*M). STRING - string, TARGET - string, DESTINATION - container. 

string-find-first-not-of STRING, TARGET, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-find-last-of
docs.text:
Attempts to find the first character found in TARGET in the string in a reverse order. Returns position if target can be found, otherwise null. Time complexity is O(N*M). STRING - string, TARGET - string, DESTINATION - container. 

string-find-last-of STRING, TARGET, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-find-last-not-of
docs.text:
Attempts to find the first character not found in TARGET in the string in a reverse order. Returns position if target can be found, otherwise null. Time complexity is O(N*M). STRING - string, TARGET - string, DESTINATION - container. 

string-find-last-not-of STRING, TARGET, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-replace
docs.text:
Attempts to find TARGET in the string and if it does, replaces it with REPLACEMENT. Time complexity is O(N*M). Throws if START < 0 || START > SIZE. STRING - dynamic string, TARGET - string or character, REPLACEMENT - string or character, START - unsigned integer. 

string-replace STRING, TARGET, REPLACEMENT, START

docs.title: string-replace-all
docs.text:
Finds all TARGETs in the string and replaces them with REPLACEMENT. Time complexity is O(N*M) to O(N*M*K) depending on how TARGET's size differs from REPLACEMENT's and on match count. Throws if REPLACEMENT is empty. STRING - dynamic string, TARGET - string or character, REPLACEMENT - string or character. 

string-replace-all STRING, TARGET, REPLACEMENT

docs.title: string-contains
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if TARGET is found in the string, else 0. Time complexity is O(N*M). STRING - string, TARGET - string or character, DESTINATION - container. 

string-contains STRING, TARGET, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-erase-all
docs.text:
Erases all characters found in CHARS from the string. Time complexity is O(N*M). STRING - dynamic string, CHARS - string or character. 

string-erase-all STRING, CHARS

docs.title: string-starts-with
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if string starts with START, else 0. STRING - string, START - string or character, DESTINATION - container. 

string-starts-with STRING, START, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-ends-with
docs.text:
Stores 1 in DESTINATION if string ends with END, else 0. STRING - string, END - string or character, DESTINATION - container. 

string-ends-with STRING, END, DESTINATION

docs.title: string-trim
docs.text:
Trims all whitespace from both sides of the string. STRING - dynamic string. 

string-trim STRING

docs.title: string-to-lower
docs.text:
Converts string to lowercase. STRING - dynamic string. 

string-to-lower STRING

docs.title: string-to-upper
docs.text:
Converts string to uppercase. STRING - dynamic string. 

string-to-upper STRING

docs.title: string-copy
docs.text:
Copies and allocates a new string into DESTINATION. STRING - string, DESTINATION - container. 

string-copy STRING, DESTINATION

docs.title: Constant evaluator
docs.text: Constant evaluator is a parse-time feature that can calculate constant math, such as memory sizes, constants and very commonly negative numbers.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Everything between brackets [] is evaluated in the constant evaluator and changed to the result in the code. It follows a different, more familiar syntax: 

main()
   println [2 + 4 * 3], ' ', [sin(pi() / 3)], ' ', [sqrt(2)];
During runtime, the code looks like this: 
println 14, ' ', 0.866, ' ', 1.414;

docs.text:

docs.title: Directives
docs.text: Directives are translator-time constructs that modify the token stream or set some interpreter configuration.

docs.title: @include
docs.text:
@include "FILE.pil"
Lexes and directly includes the file in the token stream. Guards against including the same file multiple times.

docs.title: @reg-size
docs.text:
@reg-size N
Change the register count to N for the program. Only the last statement is applied so it is recommended to define it after all includes. Does not matter where it's placed. Default is 16.

docs.title: @return-reg-size
docs.text:
@return-reg-size N
Change the return register count to N for the program. Only the last statement is applied so it is recommended to define it after all includes. Does not matter where it's placed. Default is 4.

docs.title: Enumerations
docs.text:
Enumerations are a group of similar constant named integers. They are used to define a plethora of integral constants. By default enumerations start with 0 and increment by one after each constant. Enumerations can also be set to specific integral values.

Just like constants, enumerations don't exist during the runtime and are completely replaced with their corresponding values at parse-time.

docs.title: Declaration
docs.text:
They can be defined using the enum keyword in a similar fashion to structures: 

enum ENUMERATION ( ENTRY1, ENTRY2 = INTEGER, ENTRY3... )
And in practice they look like this: 
enum Day (
   Monday = 1,
   Tuesday,
   Wednesday,
   Thursday,
   Friday,
   Saturday,
   Sunday,
)

enum Direction (
   East,
   West,
   North,
   South,
)

enum PermissionFlags (
   File        = [1 << 0], # 1
   Environment = [1 << 1], # 2
   OsExec      = [1 << 2], # 4
   Network     = [1 << 3], # 8
)

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
Enumeration values can be accessed using ENUM.ENTRY syntax. Enumeration types cannot be passed just like structures can and are purely parse-time for this reason. Enumerations cannot be converted to strings without an external array for the same reason. 

enum Direction ( East, West, North, South )

main()
   local direction, map, name;
   array-new map, "east", "west", "north", "south";

   set Direction.East, direction;
   array-at map, direction, name;
   println "Wind is blowing from ", name;

   set Direction.North, direction;
   array-at map, direction, name;
   println "Now wind is blowing from ", name;
   free map;

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: Functions are reusable pieces of code that can be called from anywhere in the program. A PIL file consists solely from functions and function calls. Each program starts with the main function. Code outside of functions is not permitted and not ran.

docs.title: Declaration
docs.text:
To declare a function, you need an unique identifier followed by parentheses with an optional parameter list: 

NAME(PARAM1?, PARAM2?...)
   BODY...
In practice it looks like this: 
my-hello-world()
   println "Hello, World!";

my-add(a, b)
   add a, b, $0;
   return $0;

docs.title: Calling
docs.text:
To call a function follow its identifier by the arguments to pass to it. Function calls must be terminated by a semicolon. 

main()
   my-hello-world;
   my-add 523, 814;
   println r$0;

Arguments pass copies to trivial objects (integer, floats, characters) and copies of references to allocated objects (arrays, maps, file handles) and such containers cannot be passed, only the underlying value. If a function has to return a value without a return, a solution could be to pass an integer and then set the register at the integer with reg-set built-in. 

add-copy(a, b, r)
   add a, b, $0;
   reg-set r, $0;

Functions can also be called using some built-ins, such as call, func-call and catch. Call supports named returns and all support argument passing. Each is used for their own case.

docs.title: Returning
docs.text:
To return values from a function, use the return bulit-in. You can return as many values as you'd like (as long as you have enough return registers). Some return built-ins are available such as the return-count, which returns the returned value count.

A function can return a variable amount of values based on different paths. Returned variables can either be accessed via return registers or return built-ins. 

get-some(condition)
   jmp condition, get-some-more;
   return 1, 2;
get-some-more:
   return 1, 2, 3, 4;

main()
   get-some 0;
   return-count $0;
   printfln "{}: {},{}", $0, r$0, r$1; # 2: 1,2

   get-some 1;
   return-count $0;
   printfln "{}: {},{},{},{}", $0, r$0, r$1, r$2, r$3; # 4: 1,2,3,4

docs.title: Structures
docs.text: Structures are user-defined data types with multiple named fields. They can be used to nicely organize data and are a must in larger projects.

docs.title: Declaration
docs.text:
Structures can be defined using the struct keyword: 

struct array? STRUCTURE ( FIELD1, FIELD2... )
In practice it looks like this: 
struct Vec2 ( x, y )
struct Rectangle ( x, y, width, height )
struct Level (
   player,
   obstacles,
   enemies,
   collectedCoins,
   coinCount,
   boundaries,
)

Structures are arrays under the hood. By default array functionality is disabled and none of the array built-ins work with objects. To enable this functionality, add array keyword after struct. This will enable all array built-ins. Be careful with this, as using an invalid field will result in undefined behavior. 

struct array MyArray ( a, b, c, d, e )

docs.title: Creation
docs.text:
Objects can be created using the make built-in. You must pass the same number of arguments as the amount of fields the structure has. No field can be left uninitialized (unless using structure arrays and then initializing them yourself). This allocates the object. 

global null;

main()
   local v, r, l;
   make Vec2, v, 2.5, 6.2;
   make Rectangle, r, 0.2, 6.4, 10.0, 20.0;
   make Level, l, null, null, null, 0, 0, null;
   println v;
   println r;
   println l;
   free v, r, l;

docs.title: Freeing
docs.text: Since objects are allocated, they must also be deallocated manually using free or deep-free built-ins. This can be seen in the previous example.

docs.title: Field access
docs.text:
To access and modify fields, suffix the variable with a dot and the name of the field. Using field access, you can also directly write to the object. 

struct Vec2 ( x, y )
struct Pair ( first, second )

main()
   local v1, v2, pair;
   make Vec2, v1, 1.0, 2.0;
   printfln "({}, {})", v1.x, v1.y;
   make Vec2, v2, 4.0, 3.0;
   printfln "({}, {})", v2.x, v2.y;

   make Pair, pair, v1, v2;
   printfln "({}, {})", pair.first, pair.second;
   free v1, v2;

   set 13, pair.first;
   set 37, pair.second;
   printfln "({}, {})", pair.first, pair.second;
   free pair;

docs.title: Values
docs.text: A value holds a specific type of data. A container can hold any type of value and can dynamically change during runtime.

docs.title: Values
docs.text: Name Example Description Integer12364-bit signed integer Floating123.456Double, most likely 64 bits Character'a'A single character Constant string"Hello, World!"Parse-time constant string Dynamic stringstring-new "Hello, World!", $0Allocated runtime string Function pointermainPointer to a function LabellabelPointer to a label Local variablelocalNamed container that holds a value Register$0Index of a register that holds a value Return registerr$0Index of a return register that holds a value Arrayarray-new $0, 1, 2, 3Dynamically allocated array of dynamic size Mapmap-new $0, 1, 2Allocated hash map File handlefile-open "my.file", 'r', $0A file handle Structurestruct Struct (...)A user-defined structure Structure AccessStruct.FieldAccess into a structure Global VariableglobalNamed container that holds a value Nullto-int "", $0Invalid/error value

docs.title: Value classification
docs.text: Values program-wise are split in 3 types: parse-time, runtime and container values. Container values simultaneously go under runtime values.

docs.title: Parse-time values
docs.text: Parse-time values are basic values that are able to be created at parse-time. These include integers, floating-point numbers, characters and constant strings.

docs.title: Runtime values
docs.text: Runtime values are values that must be allocated to use or require references usable after parsing. These include dynamic strings, arrays, maps, file handles, function pointers, labels and null. All except null are simply references to internal values and have to be copied explicitly (if allowed by the data type).

docs.title: Containers
docs.text: Containers are runtime values that store other values. These include registers, return registers, locals, globals and structure accesses. Constants do not fall under this category as they do not exist after parsing.

docs.title: Built-in value terminology
docs.text: Built-in documentation uses the following terminology to name a group of types.

docs.title: Stringifyable values
docs.text: Stringifyable values refer to values whose underlying data can be converted to a string. These include any type except for maps and file handles.

docs.title: Key value
docs.text: Key values are any value that can be used as a key for a hash map. These are any value except for arrays, maps and file handles.

docs.title: String value
docs.text: String value refers to any string value - constant or dynamic string, unless specifically noted as only a constant or dynamic string.

docs.title: Unsigned integer
docs.text: Unsigned integer is an integer that cannot be negative. It still is signed under the hood but when passed to a built-in it must not be negative.

docs.title: String types
docs.text: There are two types of strings - constant strings and dynamic strings. Constant strings are strings defined in quotes and they live for the entirety of the program and do not need to be deallocated. Dynamic strings, on the other hand, are returned by some of the built-ins and they must be deallocated manually.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text: Variables are containers that can store a value. A variable doesn't have a type tied to it and can store any value, that can dynamically change during runtime.

docs.title: Locals
docs.text:
Locals are variables that are purely local to a function. There are two types of locals - function parameters and locals defined by local keyword. Locals cannot be used outside of the function they are defined in. By default locals are set to null value.

Local define is a parse-time construct and so a local define is available by any path after the point it is defined. This means same local defines in a switch statement are not permitted, since local does not care about the control flow of the function. 

func(a, b)
   local c, d;
   goto skip;
   local e;
skip:
   # e is valid here, even though local was never touched.

docs.title: Globals
docs.text:
Globals are variables that can be accessed by any part of the program after the point it is defined. A global defined inside a function is still accessible to all functions and commands after it, although it is not recommended to do so.

Globals can be defined using global keyword. Just like locals, globals are parse-time constructs, but unlike locals, can be assigned an initial value. By default globals are set to null value. Unlike constants, their value can change during runtime. Global constructs can be chained using commas, with the last one ending with a semicolon. 

global my-global = 1337;
global other-global;

main()
   set 42, other-global;
   println my-global, ' ', other-global;

docs.title: Constants
docs.text:
Constants are values that cannot change during runtime. They are also parse-time constructs that are completely erased before runtime begins. They can be defined using const keyword similarly to globals, but must have a value. 

const my-const = 1337, pi = 3.141592;

main()
   println my-const, ' ', pi;

docs.title: Registers/return registers
docs.text:
By default there are 16 registers and 4 return registers for a program. But that can be changed using Directives. Registers are global containers that do not need to be defined. They should be used for temporary, unimportant values such as conditions. They can be accessed using $N and r$N syntax respectively and are 0-indexed. By default registers are set to null value.

Registers cannot be accessed using runtime values but can be using parse-time constructs such as constants and enumerations. This can be used to create named registers, which is equal to globals. The only reason for this could be the register built-ins.

Return registers are set by the return built-in, which is added at the end of every function if it is not already present. Return registers are set in the same order they are returned and can be read and modified just like regular registers. Return registers are not cleared if a function returns less than previously, instead a flag is set to the return count of the function, which can be retrieved with the return-count built-in. If more values are returned than there are return registers, parse-time error is thrown and they must be bumped up using @return-reg-size directive. 

const cond = 0;

my-min(a, b)
   le a, b, $cond;
   jmp $cond, my-min-a-less;
   return b;
my-min-a-less:
   return a;

main()
   my-min 10, 20;
   println r$0;
